story.en: RouteIQ product team weekly sync. Divya clicks through slides and stops: "I need routes that are performing above average. Specifically, routes where the average travel time is higher than the overall average across all routes. Those are our slow routes — optimization priority."
story.ta: RouteIQ product team weekly sync. Divya slides click panni oru slide-la nirukka: "Above average perform panra routes venum. Specifically, overall average travel time-kku mela average travel time irukara routes venum. Avangaa slow routes — optimization priority."
story.hi: RouteIQ product team weekly sync. Divya slides click karte karte ek par ruk gayi: "Mujhe above average perform karne wale routes chahiye. Specifically, woh routes jahan average travel time overall average se zyada ho. Woh hamare slow routes hain — optimization priority."
story.te: RouteIQ product team weekly sync. Divya slides click chestundi oka slide lo aagipoyindi: "Above average perform chestunna routes kavali. Specifically, overall average travel time kante ekkuva average travel time unna routes kavali. Avi slow routes — optimization priority."

question.en: Find routes where the average travel time is above the overall average travel time across all routes. Show route name and its average travel time rounded to 1 decimal place. Sort by average travel time descending.
question.ta: Ella routes-oda overall average travel time-kku mela average travel time irukara routes-a kaanu. Route name-um average travel time (1 decimal)-um kaanu. Average time highest-irundhu sort pannanum.
question.hi: Woh routes dhundho jahan average travel time overall average se zyada ho. Route naam aur average travel time 1 decimal mein dikhao. Highest se sort karo.
question.te: Anni routes overall average travel time kante ekkuva average travel time unna routes ni kanuggonu. Route peru mariyu average travel time 1 decimal lo chupinchu. Highest nundi sort cheyyali.

title.en: First find the overall average travel time
title.ta: Mudhalula overall average travel time kaanu
title.hi: Pehle overall average travel time nikalo
title.te: Mundu overall average travel time chudandi

steps.sql:
SELECT ROUND(AVG(travel_time_mins), 1) AS overall_avg
FROM route_logs;

explain.en: AVG() calculates the mean of all values in the column. This single number is your baseline. Any route with an average above this number needs attention. We will use this result as a subquery inside the main query.
explain.ta: AVG() column-la irukara ella values-oda mean calculate pannum. Ee single number oru baseline. Idal mela average irukara routes-a investigate pannanum. Idae main query-la subquery-aa use pannuvom.
explain.hi: AVG() column ke saare values ka mean nikalta hai. Yeh single number tumhara baseline hai. Isse zyada average wale routes ko dhyan dena hoga. Ise main query mein subquery ki tarah use karenge.
explain.te: AVG() column lo anni values mean calculate chestundi. Ee single number mana baseline. Ee value kante ekkuva average unna routes ni investigate cheyyali. Deetni main query lo subquery ga use cheyyali.

title.en: Use that as a subquery inside HAVING
title.hi: Ise HAVING mein subquery ki tarah use karo
title.te: Deetni HAVING lo subquery ga use cheyyandi

steps.sql:
SELECT
  route_name,
  ROUND(AVG(travel_time_mins), 1) AS avg_travel_time
FROM route_logs
GROUP BY route_name
HAVING AVG(travel_time_mins) > (
  SELECT AVG(travel_time_mins) FROM route_logs
)
ORDER BY avg_travel_time DESC;

explain.en: The subquery inside HAVING runs first and returns the overall average. The outer query then groups by route and checks whether each route's average exceeds that number. A subquery returning exactly one value like this is called a scalar subquery. Divya now has her slow routes list for the optimization team.
explain.ta: HAVING-la irukara subquery mudhalila run aayi overall average return pannum. Outer query appuram route-vari group panni, prathi route-oda average adha thaandum-aa nu check pannum. Exactly oru value return panra idha mathiri subquery-a scalar subquery nu soluvom. Divya-ku ipo slow routes list kedaichuchu.
explain.hi: HAVING ke andar subquery pehle run hoti hai aur overall average return karti hai. Outer query phir routes ke hisaab se group karke check karti hai ki kya har route ka average us number se zyada hai. Exactly ek value return karne wali subquery ko scalar subquery kehte hain. Divya ke paas ab optimization team ke liye slow routes list hai.
explain.te: HAVING lo subquery mundu run avvadam overall average return chestundi. Outer query appudu route vari group chesi, prathi route average aa number kante ekkuvaa ani check chestundi. Exactly oka value return chese ee lanti subquery ni scalar subquery antaamu. Divya ki ipo optimization team ki slow routes list dorikindi.

story.en: RouteIQ operations review. Divya presents the problem clearly: "Traffic congestion changes throughout the day. Classify each hour as Morning Rush (7-10), Afternoon Lull (11-16), Evening Rush (17-21), or Night (rest). Then give me average delay per city per time category. That is how we plan traffic control resources."
story.ta: RouteIQ operations review. Divya clearly explain pannandaa: "Traffic congestion time of day-vari different-aa irukku. Prathi hour-a Morning Rush (7-10), Afternoon Lull (11-16), Evening Rush (17-21), Night (rest)-aa classify pannum. Appuram prathi city-ku prathi time category-ku average delay kaanu. Adha vachchu traffic resources plan pannuvom."
story.hi: RouteIQ operations review. Divya ne clearly explain kiya: "Traffic congestion time of day ke hisaab se alag hoti hai. Har hour ko Morning Rush (7-10), Afternoon Lull (11-16), Evening Rush (17-21), ya Night (baaki) classify karo. Phir har city aur time category ke liye average delay do. Isi se traffic resources plan karenge."
story.te: RouteIQ operations review. Divya clearly explain chesindi: "Traffic congestion time of day vari different ga untundi. Prathi hour ni Morning Rush (7-10), Afternoon Lull (11-16), Evening Rush (17-21), Night (migulaavi) ga classify cheyyali. Appudu prathi city ki prathi time category ki average delay ivvali. Adi vachchi traffic resources plan cheyyali."

question.en: Classify trips by hour into Morning Rush (7-10), Afternoon Lull (11-16), Evening Rush (17-21), or Night (rest). Find average delay per city per time category rounded to 1 decimal. Order by city then time category.
question.ta: Trips-a hour-vari Morning Rush (7-10), Afternoon Lull (11-16), Evening Rush (17-21), Night (rest)-la classify pannu. Prathi city-ku prathi time category-ku average delay (1 decimal) kaanu. City, appuram time category-vari sort pannanum.
question.hi: Trips ko hour ke hisaab se Morning Rush (7-10), Afternoon Lull (11-16), Evening Rush (17-21), ya Night (baaki) mein classify karo. Har city aur time category ke liye average delay 1 decimal mein do. City ke hisaab se, phir time category se sort karo.
question.te: Trips ni hour vari Morning Rush (7-10), Afternoon Lull (11-16), Evening Rush (17-21), Night (migulaavi) lo classify cheyyali. Prathi city ki prathi time category ki average delay 1 decimal lo ivvali. City vari, appudu time category vari sort cheyyali.

title.en: Classify each row into a time category using CASE WHEN
title.ta: CASE WHEN use panni prathi row-a time category-la classify pannu
title.hi: CASE WHEN se har row ko time category mein classify karo
title.te: CASE WHEN use chesi prathi row ni time category lo classify cheyyandi

steps.sql:
SELECT city, hour_of_day, delay_mins,
  CASE
    WHEN hour_of_day BETWEEN 7 AND 10  THEN 'Morning Rush'
    WHEN hour_of_day BETWEEN 11 AND 16 THEN 'Afternoon Lull'
    WHEN hour_of_day BETWEEN 17 AND 21 THEN 'Evening Rush'
    ELSE 'Night'
  END AS time_category
FROM trip_logs;

explain.en: BETWEEN a AND b is the same as >= a AND <= b — it is inclusive on both ends. CASE WHEN evaluates conditions top to bottom and stops at the first match. ELSE catches everything that did not match any WHEN — here hours 0 to 6 and 22 to 23 become Night.
explain.ta: BETWEEN a AND b nna >= a AND <= b mathiri — rendu ends-um inclusive. CASE WHEN conditions-a order-la evaluate pannum — oru match aana nairkka. ELSE yaarum match aagattathai catch pannum — inga hours 0-6 and 22-23 Night aagidum.
explain.hi: BETWEEN a AND b ka matlab >= a AND <= b hai — dono taraf se inclusive. CASE WHEN conditions ko order mein evaluate karta hai — ek match hote hi ruk jaata hai. ELSE woh sab catch karta hai jo kisi WHEN se match nahi hua — yahan hours 0-6 aur 22-23 Night ban jaate hain.
explain.te: BETWEEN a AND b ante >= a AND <= b tho equal — rendu ends inclusive. CASE WHEN conditions ni order lo evaluate chestundi — oka match avvadam tho aagipotundi. ELSE evaru match avvakapoina vattini catch chestundi — ikkade hours 0-6 mariyu 22-23 Night avutaayi.

title.en: Group by city and time category to get average delay
title.ta: City + time category group panni average delay kaanu
title.hi: City aur time category group karke average delay nikalo
title.te: City + time category group chesi average delay chudandi

steps.sql:
SELECT
  city,
  CASE
    WHEN hour_of_day BETWEEN 7 AND 10  THEN 'Morning Rush'
    WHEN hour_of_day BETWEEN 11 AND 16 THEN 'Afternoon Lull'
    WHEN hour_of_day BETWEEN 17 AND 21 THEN 'Evening Rush'
    ELSE 'Night'
  END AS time_category,
  ROUND(AVG(delay_mins), 1) AS avg_delay_mins
FROM trip_logs
GROUP BY city,
  CASE
    WHEN hour_of_day BETWEEN 7 AND 10  THEN 'Morning Rush'
    WHEN hour_of_day BETWEEN 11 AND 16 THEN 'Afternoon Lull'
    WHEN hour_of_day BETWEEN 17 AND 21 THEN 'Evening Rush'
    ELSE 'Night'
  END
ORDER BY city, time_category;

explain.en: GROUP BY can take a CASE WHEN expression directly — not just column names. We repeat the same CASE WHEN in both SELECT and GROUP BY. This is the safest approach since it works across all databases. In BigQuery and PostgreSQL you can use the alias name in GROUP BY, but in MySQL and SQLite you must repeat the full expression.
explain.ta: GROUP BY CASE WHEN expression-a directly edukkalaam — column names mattum illai. SELECT-lum GROUP BY-lum CASE WHEN-a repeat panrom. Idhu ella databases-lum work aagara safest approach. BigQuery and PostgreSQL-la GROUP BY-la alias name use pannalam, aana MySQL and SQLite-la full expression repeat pannanum.
explain.hi: GROUP BY seedha CASE WHEN expression le sakta hai — sirf column names nahi. SELECT aur GROUP BY dono mein CASE WHEN repeat karte hain. Yeh sabse safe approach hai kyunki sab databases mein kaam karta hai. BigQuery aur PostgreSQL mein GROUP BY mein alias naam use kar sakte ho, but MySQL aur SQLite mein pura expression repeat karna padta hai.
explain.te: GROUP BY directly CASE WHEN expression ni teesukogaladu — sirf column names kaadu. SELECT mariyu GROUP BY renditilo CASE WHEN ni repeat chestunnamu. Idi anni databases lo work avvutundi — most safe approach. BigQuery mariyu PostgreSQL lo GROUP BY lo alias name use cheyyavacchu, kaani MySQL mariyu SQLite lo full expression repeat cheyyali.
